newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian oil firm Rosneft says Soros has eyed stake.
newsitem.headline: Russian oil firm Rosneft says Soros has eyed stake.

text.p: U.S. financier George Soros has expressed interest in bidding for a stake in Russia's last big, wholly state-owned oil company Rosneft, a Rosneft spokesman said on Wednesday.
Soros indicated he was prepared to spend around $1 billion on the project, the spokesman added, but it was unclear how much of this might be spent on shares and how much on investment.
"There definitely has been such interest (shown by George Soros)," Vladimir Vyunitsky said. "I heard this from (Rosneft president Yuri) Bespalov. He (Bespalov) is seriously looking at this proposal."
Vyunitsky said Bespalov had seen documents showing Soros had expressed an interest in bidding for a stake, and that Bespalov had mentioned the sum of $1 billion.
"Soros is one of several companies interested in buying Rosneft. Bespalov also said that he (Soros) was interested in investing around one billion dollars," Vyunitsky said.
Vyunitsky could not say exactly how far Soros had taken his proposals or where they stood now.
"To what extent he (Soros) is interested at this very moment I can't say."
Rosneft officials said on Tuesday that 51 percent of the company would be up for sale in September, and that 97 percent of the firm is likely to be sold off in total.
They also said the firm might seek approval to scrap a law limiting foreign ownership in oil companies to 15 percent in order to win wider foreign investment.

Rosneft produced 13.1 million tonnes (262,000 barrels per day) of crude oil in 1996 from 12.8 million (256.000 bpd) in 1995. It is valued for, among other things, its status as the state's agent in production-sharing deals.
The company is the centre of a bitter ideological battle between Bespalov and board chairman Alexander Putilov, who have sharply differing views on the group's future.
Soros' interest in Rosneft follows hard on the heels of another high-budget Russian play last week.
He told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that his funds took about half the 25 percent of Russian telecommunications company Svyazinvest privatised last week, investing around $980 million.
The Svyazinvest deal took his exposure to Russia to $2.5 billion, Soros said.
He attributed renewed interest in Russia as an investment opportunity to the appointment to the government of reformist Boris Nemtsov as First Deputy Prime Minister.
